newsitem.title: USA: U.S Senate panel aims to complete FDA bill quickly.
newsitem.headline: U.S Senate panel aims to complete FDA bill quickly.

text.p: A Senate panel began work Wednesday on a bill to reform the Food and Drug Administration and extend a prescription drug user fee program that generates funds for product review at the FDA.

The Senate Labor and Human Resources Committee touched on only minor amendments and will not get into the heart of the reform until next week. But the bill has bipartisan support and chairman Jim Jeffords, a Vermont Republican, said it was his priority to get the bill through the committee and then onto the floor swiftly.
The Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) expires at the end of this fiscal year and if it is not renewed quickly about 600 FDA workers could get layoff notices in August.

The bill dropped some of the most contentious measures that were in a version of FDA reform last year. It has broad bipartisan backing in the committee, although panel members are not in agreement on all aspects of the reform plan, which would allow the FDA to use more outsiders to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of new drugs and medical devices.
